utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, you say that you do not know anything about the Law on Defence of the Republic of Croatia dated 1991. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you asked me and I'm telling you that this is the first time I see it and read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It will be most probably easy for you to take a look at Article 22, Article 23, I presume?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam Alaburic, Croatian law or --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's correct. These articles govern the powers of the government and you can compare them to the authorities of the HVO, the Ministry of Defence's powers. Would it take you a long time to go through all these?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would take me some time. I wish during my proofing you had spoken about this with me. It would be farfetched for me to give you opinions out of hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Out of what you just said, the Trial Chamber may conclude that I took part in the proofing for your testimony, but I would like you to tell everybody in the courtroom whether I took part in the proofing or not?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You did not take part in the proofing, but I said had you wished to do so, I would have been glad to talk to you about my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We will have occasion to compare those two pieces of legislation and we will see that the decree from Herceg-Bosna is a copied text of this Croatian law. I wanted to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I've tried not to interject and disturb my learned friend's flow but there is a discernible proclivity, in my respectful submission, in questions to infect them by statements of evidence. The same issue has been raised very properly by my learned friend from the Prosecution, and I would ask that my learned friend desist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Alaburic, what do you think about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, given that I worked on those regulations and I think that I know them quite well, I think that I stated something which is known to everybody and that anybody who would take a look at these two documents could find for themselves. If anybody in this courtroom thinks that I add a statement that needs proving, I apologise, this was not my intention. Your Honours, you will have both those documents, you will be able to compare them, to highlight the differences, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Alaburic, could you not ask the witness a question and say that from your point of view, i.e., the Petkovic Defence, you could have said, Well, the interpretation General Petkovic made of these documents is the following. What do you think, and the witness would say, I agree or I do not agree. And that's it. Otherwise we could go on for hours on this issue. I've tried to guide you by saying, well, we have this text, we have the other text, and regarding the legal problems the Judges will have to make a decision. You nevertheless went on. Your witness, which you are cross-examining, is someone who knows law as well as you do, so you can move on to a main question and say, Well, if I give you this interpretation of the text, would you agree with me or not, and you will see what the witness says. And like that we will be able to save time. Right, Mr. Khan?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to refresh everybody's memory in this courtroom that in the preceding weeks we had an expert witness for the Defence team of Bruno Stojic. In paragraph 131 of the expert report, Bruno Stojic's Defence expert witness said that Herceg-Bosnia regulations were copied Croatian legislation and regulations. Therefore, I believe that this is an argument which has been presented by the Defence team of Mr. Stojic to the Trial Chamber. Now I wanted to demonstrate that this was really so, and this is why I'm showing you this Croatian piece of legislation, and I believe that it is very important for interpreting a piece of legislation if you are copying a provision and you do not copy it in its entirety, this demonstrates the legislators intent. And this is all I wanted to say in connection with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to remind you of another thing concerning the Decree on the Armed Forces Mr. Marijan said and elaborated at length, the Article 178 of the Decree on the Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think there has been perhaps a misunderstanding. Mr. Khan's objection is not as to whether it is correct what Ms. Alaburic states or not, but the fact that she discusses the issue rather than asking questions. Now Ms. Nozica also starts discussing the issue and this is not what we should be doing. We should put questions to the witness and hear his answers with as little personal comment of counsel as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your Honours, as far as the claim of what Mr. Marijan said, I would like to remind the Bench because the debate continues. It did not cease and desist after my learned friend Khan's intervention. Mr. Marijan said this was a compilation of two Yugoslav laws speaking about the Decree on the Armed Forces. He specifically explained that and he invoked Article 178 of this decree, Decree on the Armed Forces of Herceg-Bosna, this is what we are referring to. And let me remind you that what Mr. Marijan wrote in his report cannot be applied to all pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will no longer dwell on this issue. I'd just like to respond to my learned friend, lead counsel of Mr. Stojic, that she misinterpreted the statement of the expert witness Marijan. But let us stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, pursuant to the Decree on the Armed Forces of Herceg-Bosnia, what were the powers and the competencies of the Main Staff of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I supposed to take a look at that part of the decree?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, could you tell me which article, I never remembered the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm going to mention the numbers of articles dealing with the Main Staff, but I don't believe they will be of help. Article 11 and 18. You may take a look at all the other articles, and please tell me what were the tasks of the General Staff pursuant to the Decree on the Armed Forces?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours. I would like to hear from my learned friends to cite which part of examination-in-chief this question is dealing with, and as far as I can remember, I never asked the witness about matters of the authority of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Simply the Decree on the Armed Forces was subject matter of your examination-in-chief. This witness was introduced to us as an expert who took part in drafting this regulation. He explained the nomotechnical problems encountered with Article 34. He explained the provision of Article 30 asked by the Defence counsel for Mr. Bozic which governs Supreme Command and powers of the General Staff are in direct connection with that, and this is why I believe my questions refer to those questions in examination-in-chief. If the Trial Chamber should decide otherwise, I will not object for the time for these questions to be deducted from my total time credit for the Defence of General Petkovic. Pursuant to your guide-lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say a couple of things, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let the transcript finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, I think you should limit yourself to answering questions because otherwise we get too far. I'm sorry, I can understand that you have the feeling that you would like to say this and that, but you are completely dependent on the questions that are put to you. Please continue, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to answer a statement, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, please answer my questions. What are the powers of the Main Staff pursuant to the Decree on the Armed Forces of Herceg-Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer I must say that you misquoted me. I said I did not work on drafting this decree. I will tell you, in Article 11 the task described under Article 10, paragraph 2 of this decree. The General Staff shall be founded within the Defence Department. Second paragraph, the structure of the General Staff shall be prescribed by the supreme commander of the armed forces who shall appoint the General Staff leadership.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, we all know how to read the law. But tell us, please, what are the powers of the General Staff pursuant to this decree? What are the powers? What is it that the General Staff may do pursuant to the provisions of this decree?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is so regulated, my opinion is that the General Staff is connected with the supreme commander of the armed forces of the HZ-HB in terms of structuring and the use of the armed forces of the Croatian community Herceg-Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, please tell us pursuant to the decree. My question is specific.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read out from the decree.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You did not read the powers. You said that General Staff is being established, but this is not contentious, but I'm asking you about the tasks of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by asking that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's see. In Article 9 it is said what are the tasks of the HVO, isn't it so? In Article 10, paragraph 1, it is stated what are the administrative and technical work in the field of defence and protection of the Defence Department. Now I'm going to ask you what are the tasks pursuant to this decree of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following your question, it would seem that the decree does not regulate or govern or specify the tasks of the General Staff, and this is an omission and I just explained to you the way that we cannot read what are the tasks of the Main Staff in the decree, but I see that through the provisions of Article 11 and the decisions on the internal structure of the General Staff adopted by Mr. Boban, and in that decision, the tasks and the functions and the functioning of the Main Staff of the HVO were regulated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So can we presume, following what you said, that the decree does not regulate the powers of the Main Staff; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be so, but I just provided a supplementary opinion on the -- with respect to the decision on the internal structure of the Defence Department which follows from the decree of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No, no. We will come to that document but please limit your answers to the decree. Is it true the decree does not govern the authorities of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, just in the same way that it regulates for the other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If it doesn't, how are these regulated?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the decision on the internal structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the decree of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which articles you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, find any article in the decree that defines the purview of the Main Staff, its powers.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this section, the administration and the affairs of the defence, the Main Staff is mentioned only in Article 11 and it's not mentioned among the powers and authorisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What about some other section?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you help me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, you certainly read this decree in your proofing. If you don't remember, tell me you don't remember and we'll go on.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, since you worked at the Defence Department have you ever come across the following legal issue, namely that regulations may stipulate wide or narrow powers of the Main Staff, or rather, that the political will may be to establish a strong Main Staff or alternatively a weak Main Staff? Have you ever given this any thought?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not, not in that way, but you have given me food for thought now. At any rate, this connection exists in this decree between the Main Staff and the supreme commander. If he is that political will, then we can talk about political will.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, we are now exclusively at the level of regulations. I'm asking you only about de jure and the political will that can be discerned from a regulation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer because I don't know which regulation you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Any regulation in the field of defence that would stipulate issues important to the Main Staff, can we agree -- sorry. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You go on, I'll answer later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we say that as far as regulations adopted by the legislator in Herceg-Bosna, that was the Decree on the Armed Forces, and that all the other decisions were decisions of the president as an individual, Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Bruno Stojic as head of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right when you say that these were the documents, the enactments, the Decree on the Armed Forces; and on the other hand, we have decrees adopted by Mate Boban speaking of the Main Staff. And speaking of Mr. Stojic, I believe the relationship between Mr. Stojic and the Main Staff is precisely defined by those "bylaws," although they are not really bylaws. Let me finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You could have answered with a yes or no. Your answer is perfectly understandable. Let's move on. What I want to say now is can you answer the question about the political will to establish a strong versus a weak Main Staff. Let's assume that the Croatian law on Defence from 1991, as far as powers of the Main Staff are concerned, was identical to the Decree on the Armed Forces of Herceg-Bosna, as we can see, by comparing the relevant articles and all the other articles in these two enactments. Now please look at the Law on Defence of the Republic of Croatia of 2002. Just as an illustration. It's 4D 1287. It's a document passed at the time when social democrats and liberals were in power. Would you please look at Article 11. In that Article 11 the powers of the Main Staff are identified in 31 items. Mr. Bozic, I won't ask you anything specific about this, I'm just using this as an illustration. Can you tell us, as a lawyer and an assistant chief of the Defence Department, that indeed from a regulation we can discern the intent of the legislator to establish a strong or a weak Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that the intent of the legislator in all instances in establishing any organ including the Main Staff, and I'm speaking about the period 1992, 1993, in Herceg-Bosna when there was a provisional authority and provisional organs, and we have to bear in mind that this was an executive power and a commander of the same nature, so it's hard to compare with well-regulated environments, but I agree with you that all these organs are an expression of the political will expressed through executive authorities. And we have to look at the specific period when this was happening in the community of Herceg-Bosna in the context of the provisional, I repeat, provisional executive power in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. We have all that in mind. You said a moment ago, Mr. Bozic, that the position of the Main Staff was actually defined by these decisions about the internal organisation of the Defence Department; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's defined by the decision on fundamental organisation, and later developed through the decision on internal organisation and the Main Staff is regulated in a special way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It's not in dispute that the Main Staff is one organisational units of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call it an organisational unit because when we lawyers speak, we have to be very precise. When we say that the Defence Department consists of these sectors and within the Defence Department there is the Main Staff, I agree with you, Main Staff, the Main Staff is within the Defence Department. That's what I would agree with.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: But the Main Staff is in part of its powers directly connected to the supreme commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And in that sense, the position of the Main Staff was two-pronged in a certain way?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It has a relationship to the chief of the Defence Department and another relationship towards the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the Chief of the Main Staff was a member of the college of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you it was not a formal body with formal membership. It's a body that met ad hoc, but somebody from the Main Staff participated and represented the Main Staff at certain sessions of the college of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The college of the head of the Defence Department was not prescribed by any particular law or regulation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct, there was no particular enactment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to conclude, maybe I'm wrong, that the chief of the Defence Department wanted to cooperate with the top people in certain sectors and the Chief of the Main Staff so that they could discuss together defence-related issues and try to find the best solutions to certain problems topical at a certain time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I explained that yesterday. I don't know how successful or how clear I was, but those were meetings held from time to time to discuss topics on which the opinion of the Chief of the Main Staff or representatives of the Main Staff was sought. If those were specific issues of interest to them, especially in preparation of documents that we prepared towards the president of Herceg-Bosna and the president of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From the documents, from the records of the college meetings, we can see that you had very strict rules of work. There was an established agenda, records were kept, you discussed certain topics of the agenda, you adopted decisions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right in part. There was an attempt to create such an organisation, such a possibility to communicate, but there were meetings, on the other hand, that were not really convened. Records were not kept, there was no established agenda because situations sometimes required some topics to be discussed ad hoc. But there were other sessions more organised with records kept, with background material provided, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, when progress reports needed to be made from, let's say, a session of the HVO, was the report of the Main Staff part of the report from the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we informed all sectors of the Defence Department and that part was part of the report to the Defence Department, but it had special status because it was delivered to the president of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna as the supreme commander and the president of the HVO HZ-HB and it was not part of the written report delivered to the sessions of the HVO HZ-HB, and it was not discussed at such, but all members of the HVO HZ-HB had access to that report of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you needed to make programme of work, was the programme of work of the Main Staff somehow included in the work programme of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same applies, I believe, to the work programme of the Main Staff, for the same reasons I already listed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In matters that are governed by the decisions on fundamental internal organisation, was the Chief of the Main Staff answerable to the chief of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was, but for a certain part of his powers and very specifically defined issues in that field.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Bozic, now tell us, was there any issue where the chief of the Defence Department was answerable to the Chief of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of your previous question when I talked about that relationship between the Chief of the Main Staff and the head of the Defence Department referred to certain technical or professional issues, and there was no document that stipulated that the head of the Defence Department would be answerable to the Chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. We've dealt with the issue of documents. In practice now, was there any situation where the Chief of the Main Staff would call the head of the Defence Department to report to him?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Bozic, that the Chief of the Main Staff was answerable to the head of the Defence Department in very specifically defined issues?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's try to define these issues because precise and exact definition of these issues is of exceptional importance for a correct understanding of the entire situation in Herceg-Bosna for the Trial Chamber and for all of us in the courtroom. Now, tell me, the establishment of military units, in section 8 of my binder, Mr. Bozic, you have documents for some of these issues. I hope we won't have to open them, but just open section 8 to be ready.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see an 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It's a batch of documents marked 8, the one but last section.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it says, "Basic organisation of the Defence Department"?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It starts with document 586, correct. But perhaps there won't be any need to look at it. Tell me, was the establishment of military units within the purview of the head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to bear in mind one fact that you all know, Judges, namely, that the military units were set up even before the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, I'm not asking for an historical overview of the establishment of the HVO. I just want you to tell me whether the establishment of military units, brigades, and other units was in the purview, within the field of competence of the head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I need to look at a document?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: First tell me if you remember.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Look at P 491. These are randomly chosen documents.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: P 491, order by Bruno Stojic, dated 16 September 1992, relating to the establishment of brigades. Now look at the next document, P 517, an order by Bruno Stojic, also September 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: P 517. Establishment of brigades and the Mostar sector. Next document, P 3149, an order by Bruno Stojic and Milivoje Petkovic, dated 3rd July 1993, to establish the Knez Domagoj Brigade. Believe me, we have dozens of these documents. If your memory is refreshed, was the establishment of brigades and other military units within the field of competence of the head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. You probably have in mind some specific provision I can't remember, but I see here various orders signed jointly by the Chief of the Main Staff and head of the Defence Department so obviously in practice these things happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can I then conclude that you, in fact, don't know whether the establishment of military units was within the purview of the head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely because if you referred me to a particular provision, it would be easier; but as I said, practice shows that it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bozic, I'm not going to show you individual provisions of the decree so that you may confirm that this has been governed so by the decree. We will read the decree ourselves. What we want you, as a witness, deputy head of the Defence Department, to tell us whether certain things were within the purview of the head of the Defence Department or not. Next question concerns the issues of public law and order. Was maintaining public law and order part of the purview of the head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally and legally I would say no, but having in mind the realistic situation on the ground and given that there were many people out in the streets wearing military uniforms, sometimes it was necessary for the minister or, rather, head of the department for the interior, together with the head of the Defence Department to resolve such issues as may have cropped up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, if maintaining law and order that may be disrupted by military personnel and the Defence Department was not in charge of that, which other organ would have competence in this case?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for military personnel, the Defence Department would be supposed to be in charge of them, but I'm explaining you a situation where civilians wore military uniforms, and as lawyers, we must say that somebody is not a military personnel if they are wearing a uniform. They are civilians in military clothes. But taking stock of the situation on the ground at the time, I believe it was helpful for the department of the interior and the Department of Defence to jointly tackle such issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could you take a look at the document corroborating what you said, the fourth in this section, P 2578. This is an exhibit in these proceedings. This is a joint order of the head of the Defence Department, and the head of the department of the interior, dated 31st of May, 1993, concerning controls on exits from Mostar in connection with looting of property and transfer of such property outside of Mostar. Is this order an example of what you just described to us, Mr. Bozic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an example of what I just said and given that I had worked in the police before, assuming my position in the Defence Department, and since I yesterday said to the Chamber that I, although a civilian, also wore a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall whether the control over combat of readiness over certain military units was part of the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand your question. I'm sorry. What do you mean by control over combat readiness?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I will quote Article 17 on the decree of the armed forces: "The combat readiness of the headquarter staff's institutions and units of the armed forces is controlled and assessed by the Department of Defence and the authorised commands and staffs of the armed forces." So I'm asking you whether the control over the combat readiness of certain units was within the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commenting such a provision as read out loud here, the answer is clear but practice shows how this was operationalised. I agree with you that this provision governs the matter in this way. I have to apologise, I'm not a military expert. I did my military service at a time and that was it. But when discussing combat readiness and what it entails, I would like to say to Their Honours that I cannot assess combat readiness, whether it is equipment, materiel or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next document, P 1418. This is a report on the control of combat readiness, dated 4th of February, 1993, submitted to the head of the Defence Department, chief of the General Staff and the commander of the operational zone, concerning the line of defence at Konjic.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the beginning of paragraph 1(a). It is stated there that Defence line of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade and the 7th Suad Alic Brigade of the BH Army were visited. This is February 1993. Does this -- does it follow from this that together the HVO and the BH Army are together manning the line of defence?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does it follow from this document that this was an example of controlling whether the defence line has been secured pursuant to the professional regulations?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but let's take a look at the preamble of this report, which says pursuant to the order of the Chief of the Main Staff, so and so number, this control is being carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I will hark back to Article 17 which say that the Defence Department in cooperation with commands and staffs will do so, so of course the Defence Department did form such tasks in cooperation with other bodies. The next question concerns the relocation and accommodation of military units. Would this fall within the purview of the head of the Defence Department, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, yes, these would be matters of logistics administration, supplies, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Control of traffic, checkpoints, such issues, would those follow within the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going back to the situation and the time when this unfolded and I must tell you that we should be mindful that most of the people that walked around in military uniforms and that the Defence Department had to tackle, together with the civilian police and civilian authorities, such issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Security matters dealt with by the SIS, were they also matters falling within the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the sector for security is one of the sectors within the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that SIS work was part of the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you what this entails. I never analysed the structure and the scope of work of other sectors apart from the sector that I dealt with and that was the civilian affairs sector. If I were to say anything else, it would be speculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's follow a logic, Mr. Bozic. Did SIS perform the task within its purview?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was the SIS a sector within the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'd like to correct the transcript in line 20, my question should be deleted because in line 21, my question was registered and recorded there. On the current page, line 20, I don't know how it ended up on this page. Mr. Bozic, you said that the SIS was a sector within the Defence Department. Would it be logical that work of the SIS which is performed by the -- within the Defence Department would fall within the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that there was an assistant head for security and information and the SIS was a sector within the department of the defence. This is an administration within a sector which is very important to point out. If you wish to discuss this with me and your goal is for me to frank, if I had known what the structure was and how it was elaborated, I would have been very glad to answer those questions, but I maintain that I did not know anything about the structures and the relationship within the structures of other sectors. I cannot comment on those. Whatever I may offer as an opinion would be speculation and I do not wish to speculate in front of this Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, for your information, you have four minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. Tell us, please, did military police affairs within -- fall within the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military police affairs were within the purview of the military police administration, and I don't want to comment on what were the relationship and the structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you in terms of organisational chart. We all know all of that. I'm asking you about the functioning, the functional connections. I am asking you whether military police tasks were within the purview of the Defence Department or some other organ of the Herceg-Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say yes, I mean that military police will regulate traffic, that they would apprehend a soldier who is acting inappropriately, that they would apprehend perpetrators of criminal offences, and as a lawyer, I interpret their tasks to be as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Were the tasks within the moral education department, were they within the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the Department of Defence, there was a sector for moral upbringing as a sector within the structure of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, we know that, but please answer the question, whether those tasks were part of the purview of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I have to intervene. The witness said, "I cannot comment on what was elsewhere in the other sectors, I do not want to speculate," and he's uttered those words twice. "I can comment on what I was in charge." Further questions are a waste of time because the witness is obviously going to answer in the same vein.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very glad to hear that Madam Nozica knows what is the witness is going to answer to my questions, but I would like to say, however, that I'm not asking the witness about anything within the administration of SIS and the administration of military police. I'm talking to him about the issues falling within the purview of the Defence Department which he, as the deputy head of the Defence Department, should know; and if he does not know anything, then the Judges will evaluate his testimony in the way that they see fit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will answer any question that you may ask. You, nor Madam Nozica, neither I can say how I'm going to answer until asked. I would like to say I am witness to justice as Judge Antonetti said, and whatever I say I say because I knew about those things because I witnessed them, because I worked on them. I do not wish to speculate. Please do not bring me into a situation where although I underwent proofing with Madam Nozica that she would know how I'm going to answer. Ultimately, I will wish to be the witness to justice and I want to maintain my identical relationship towards all the six co-accused here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I do not doubt it Mr. Bozic. Had I doubted it, I would not have spent so much time discussing these matters with you. My last question, the health sector, health care for the wounded and other issues of health, were they also part of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Health sector is part of the Defence Department. I confirm that it was a sector within the Defence Department. I do not know how the system within that sector was organised. Since this is your last question, I must tell that you I was deputy head of the Defence Department who had very specific duties and authorities which concerned exclusively the civilian sector. Had I had other authorities and knowledge, I would have answered differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, for the time you've given me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bozic, for your answers. I read your statement to the Prosecution. I accept that you were in charge of the civilian sector and this is why I did not ask any questions concerning other sectors within the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mrs. Alaburic. Mr. Khan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Just one clarification, with your leave. At page 67, line 20, my learned friend Ms. Alaburic appears to have misunderstand the nature of my leader's intervention. It was not anticipatory or seeking to predict what the witness would say. My learned friend's objection was referenced on what the witness had said in the past. It was on that basis that she said that the further questions given the witness's testimony that he was not confident on what was the organisation of other structures was based. So I think that clarification perhaps should be recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is in the transcript. Mr. Karnavas, anything? Or we were dealing with D4, we can do D5, D6, D1, just as you want. Well, for Mr. Coric. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I start my cross, I would like to ask the witness to be as slow as possible during the break. They asked me from the interpreter's booth to make a pause after my question. You will see on the screen the question entering the transcript, and I will of course, after your answer, make a pause so that everything is reflected in the transcript. Have you understood?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to follow-up on what Madam Alaburic said towards the end of her cross-examination. I'd like to ask whether I understood you correctly when you said in examination-in-chief and in cross-examination today saying that your knowledge from the relevant time concern work in the civilian sector of the Defence Department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Any extra knowledge that you may recall concern exclusively the meetings that you attended; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: When you said to my learned friend Alaburic about what were the tasks of the military police, as far as I could understand, you concluded that on the basis of your own knowledge and following a certain logic, following a lawyer's logic, without being privy to the documents of the time or orders of the time concerning how the military police is organised, how it's structured, the way of command of a military police. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You understood me correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Given that there was talk today about certain documents whose authenticity is being contested, and as far as I can see you had some knowledge about that, I would like to show you a document, the middle document, P 3220, a document in the middle of my binder, and before it's going called up, I would like to ask you whether you know Mr. Coric and Mr. Radovan Lavric's signatures; do you know?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the signature of Mr. Coric looked like since his documents reached the Defence Department when college meetings were being prepared. I know Mr. Lavric because while I was chief of police in Mostar, Mr. Lavric was head of the police station in Ljuboski and towards the end of 1993 when the Office for Cooperation with UNPROFOR, EC Monitoring Mission and other international organisations was being set up, Mr. Lavric and I worked together. He was my deputy. We are still friends, we meet frequently, both because of professional obligations and privately, and I know how his signature looked like from the time that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, look at the document in front of you are or on the monitor. Have you seen it before? Do you know anything about it and is it Lavric's signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see this document before but I heard a comment about it because I meet with Mr. Lavric who's a good friend of mine at least once a month and for business even more frequently, because we both work in our own companies, and I think -- in fact, I remember clearly it was in the first quarter around Easter, perhaps, 2007. We found -- we met somewhere in Medjurgorje at a luncheon and he told me, "You are not the only one who has forgeries, there are forgeries with my own signature," and he was talking about those two days when he -- when documents appeared related to the defence office in Jablanica because at that time we worked together at the office in Mostar. And he told me that in talks with you somebody from the Coric team mentioned a document allegedly sent to Colonel Obradovic relating to prisons, and he said he had not signed that document and some other details which he repeated to me recently when we met, and he knew I was coming here; and he said they had no communication, they from the military police, they had no communications from the prisons in Gabela and Dretelj and the only connection between the military in Dretelj was through the barracks, which is physically separate from the prison compound, something that I wouldn't know because I haven't been there myself. And I'm stating here before the Court what Mr. Lavric told me. And he also told me that that was not his signature and that a certain document that your team has presented bears his forged signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic, I may again be disoriented or stupid or something, but I hear speaking of the signature of Mr. Lavric, and I think the document is P 03220, and I don't find that signature on these. There are two photocopies of B/C/S documents, and perhaps you could help me find this signature. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] I'll explain, Your Honour. We see typewritten words Valentin Coric; however, in this case, some documents have been admitted in evidence and what is handwritten looks like Lavric's signature, that's why we contacted Mr. Lavric because on the face of it, this looks like some of his, indisputably, his signatures. However, he says -- I mean, I don't know what he will testify, but these signatures are very much alike, and the witness has information from Mr. Lavric directly, and he told you what it was because this is certainly not the signature of Mr. Coric. It looks most like Lavric's signature. And Mr. Lavric was a deputy of Mr. Coric at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. It does not look like it was signed by someone else for Mr. Coric. Normally there is then mention for "rodja" [phoen] something like that, and this I do not see. That is had he why I thought it purported actually to be the signature of Mr. Coric, whereas Mr. Lavric is never mentioned even by name in either of these documents. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you look at the stamp more carefully, I have a better copy here if you want it, to the left of letter V in Coric's name, we see that there is an illegibly written Z and A. But we can see that something it written on this stamp on top of the letters O S in the word Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us try to understand. If I understand correctly, the document we have here is a forged document. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Yes. And since I received this information from Mr. Lavric, I got up every time in the courtroom and repeated the same thing. This is perhaps not the time to say this, this is something I should discuss with my witnesses later; but there are other indications that what I'm saying is right. Namely, the log-book of Heliodrom which has been admitted into evidence and this document was never received there. But I repeat, I will have a witness who is directly linked to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that more clearly now. This document P 3220 has probably been admitted. Okay. We'll take note of that. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to a different subject now. Mr. Bozic, how often were college meetings held at the Defence Department, those informal meetings you spoke about.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends. I said sometimes they would be held a couple of times a month, sometimes they were well prepared with the agenda and background material, as I told Mrs. Alaburic; sometimes that there was no agenda, depending on what the situation called for.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: At some of those college meetings, Mr. Coric attending; right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: At these college meetings, was it possible, and it would seem natural to me, to ask questions of any member of the college, ask for a report, put an objection to his work if there were any problems or if something needed to be discussed from the area of work of each sector.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of those meetings was to exchange information and to pass certain documents that would go through further procedure to see who needs to do what, to distribute obligations, and under the heading current issues, you could discuss any matter at all, even if there was a set agenda.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from these college meetings, were there even more informal or less formal meetings? Because you were in the same buildings, was it possible to go at any time to anyone's office to ask a question, to talk?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I said that to Mrs. Alaburic to her question about possibilities for communication, and I can answer the same to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the department of military police issued daily, weekly, monthly reports or bulletins?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they did issue bulletins. I don't know whether they were weakly or monthly but bulletins were certainly issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who are the recipients or who had access to them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would really be guessing if told that you. I know that I saw some of them, I read some of them, but who were the recipients, I couldn't say. I don't remember that. If you showed me a bulletin, perhaps I would tell you something more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Was this bulletin available to anyone within the Security Sector and the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I saw some of them, and I had occasion to read some of them. I suppose others did too. I can't be sure, but I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us that there were semi-annual and annual reports that would later be included in the similar reports of the Defence Department; the military police department wrote semi-annual and annual reports?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These reports were part of the summary report made by the Defence Department and delivered to the HVO HZ-HB for further procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, while you were working at the Defence Department, did you ever see an order or an instruction addressed either to the military police department or Mr. Coric personally concerning taking specific action in prisons in HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't remember seeing any such order.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear a verbal order of that kind?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN BOZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination. Thank you, Mr. Bozic, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Well, before the break, let us see what you have to say, Mr. Ibrisimovic, will you have any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps during the break we can consult and then give you an answer after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We would welcome a break as well for that purpose of consulting with our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough. So let's have a 20-minute break. We'll meet in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Speaking of the position of the Pusic Defence and the examination of the other Defence teams our position is as you stated at the beginning of the session, so we have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ibrisimovic. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours. For the sake of brevity, I won't repeat what Mr. Ibrisimovic just said, but we take the same position. There will be no cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Very well. The Office of the Prosecutor has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, all those in and around the courtroom. Your Honour, I'm going to start off by asking the Court's indulgence on a number of grounds. By all indications, we appear to be based on past experience and on the schedule that we've been given, ahead of schedule a bit. I also note that today just in the course of this morning, the Prosecution has been handed several hundreds of pages of documents that we've just received for the first time. Second, further, Your Honour, I can tell that you based on the examinations conducted by Ms. Alaburic and to so some extent by the Coric Defence there's substantial overlap with some of the outlines of that that we have prepared or anticipated, and we are still also in the process of adding a few documents, although I have to -- Ms. Winner and her team were so efficient that we could get most of the binders together and distributed during the break. But all that leads me to the past, Your Honour, Prosecution would ask the Chamber's indulgence to begin cross-examination tomorrow morning rather than starting today for all those reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I can't agree. I can't agree, Mr. Scott. This is my personal opinion, but I can't agree. We have time constraints. Significant ones. You have five hours at your disposal. After you, Ms. Nozica will probably have some questions to ask to the witness during the redirect process, then Mr. Praljak will take the floor, and the witness too, he also has time constraints. As the Prosecutor in this case, I'm not going to tell you what you should be doing, but you should be in a position at least to start the cross-examination on a certain number of issues. You have one hour left today, that shouldn't be any problem with you, and then you could continue tomorrow to do the rest of the cross-examination. I'm sure there are things that you are ready to address now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, obviously I'm in the Chamber's hands, that goes without saying. Cross-examination is not a matter of taking certain questions randomly. There is a certain order that makes sense and a certain order. The order in which it was prepared is the part that directly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you wish. Hold on, hold on. We are going to confer and then we will hand over a decision. And then I will let you know what the decision of the Trial Chamber is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has deliberated. It was complicated, but the Trial Chamber decides that the cross-examination will start tomorrow from 9.00 a.m., and the Prosecution will be invited to use as best as it could the time allotted to it. We'll meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
